title: The coating and the route
bodyMd:
A fictional boat operator tested a new hull coating intended to reduce drag. Fuel use fell on the first month’s trips, but the crew had also switched to a calmer route and carried lighter loads. The supplier attributed the entire reduction to the coating. The operator requested a comparison using similar loads and routes before accepting that estimate.

This request did not deny that the coating might work. It distinguished a plausible mechanism from a measured contribution. A useful comparison would not need to reproduce every detail of every voyage, but it should address the major differences capable of affecting fuel consumption. The operator also wanted records across several months, since a coating’s initial condition might not represent its performance after prolonged use.
